shared-needs.rule: shared/ belongs to the shared author (brief C, "What R-03 produces"); this volume never writes it and never points into it before it exists. Each need names the volume and the anchor the shared author declares, using the anchor name of the node that owns the thing (envelope and cas from N-01, record-kinds-registry from N-18, codes from N-43, break-glass from N-27). check.sh (N-46) resolves a need by volume and anchor once the shared volume lands, so a need becomes a live pointer without a hand edit. The same needs are returned to the shared author as data by the seat that wrote this volume.
shared-needs.need: Rows for machine.rendered 200; selection.recorded 201; machine.not-found 404; view.invalid 422; machine.stale 503; machine.view-timeout 504. Owner-acts: none.

A lamp column per code (green, amber or red) so a screen draws a code without a table of its own; N-37 generates bindings from it and the machine panel's header lamp and the last-records chips read it.
The record envelope every kind carries: id, at (UTC), code, kind, node, attempt where one applies; this node reads and writes records only inside it.
idempotency(key PRIMARY KEY, seq, response JSON, at); a seen key replays its response with code 200.

The record kinds registry (every kind with its code set, writer node and schema path, loaded by N-43 with the code table) carries the kinds this node reads and writes: node.state (the node's state frame inside pushed.frame), selection, lease, heartbeat, seat.result, attempt; machine.panel is drawn and never stored.
leases(key, holder, token, expires_at): every lease on the selected node is listed with its fencing token and expiry; the panel never shows one current seat.
heartbeats(lease, at, seq): the heartbeat age the panel shows per lease, read from the table through N-31, never computed on the page.
A write carrying a stale fencing token is 412 and is logged; the panel shows the token so a 412 in the last records is readable against it.
No cog: every wait has a timeout and a fallback, nothing starts by an agent typing, no agent is a gate; the system drives (brief C rule 3).
Many agents at once from the first line: append-only records, compare-and-swap, idempotent retryable steps, conflicts that report as 409 (brief C rule 2).
Every automated step retries up to 3 times with backoff, then recovers and reports as a record; a dead record becomes exactly one card.
Push transport for everything; a client re-reads full state on reconnect and drops any frame older than the one it holds (D21).

purpose.s: Inspect one node: its id and spec book pointer, status code and meaning, heartbeat age against its bound, current ticket and seat, input and output records, attempt and lease, checklist with proofs, timeout and fallback, the last records and the last five alerts, and the runbook pointer (wireframe-brief.json screen Machine; C32 approved).
Primary action: open the runbook. The panel is read-only; the owner acts only on Controls (N-42) and acks only on Alerts (N-41).

input.s: The selection record (N-38, or N-41 when the owner taps an alert row) names the node; the pushed.frame (N-31) carries that node's state frame: the latest record per kind the node writes, its heartbeat records, its lease, its attempt, its checklist state (from the ticket records that cite the node's checklist anchors), and the node's open alerts.
Static parts come from the registry (N-37): the spec anchor, the runbook anchor, the input and output record kinds, the timeout and fallback text generated from the node volume's #waits section.

output.s: machine.panel is the drawn frame for one node; it is not stored. The only store writes from this screen are a selection record when the owner follows a belt to a neighbour machine (same shape as N-38's) and the client's frame.report. Opening the runbook opens the repo viewer link read-only.

panels.panel: Breadcrumb (Map, group, node), big lamp, name, status chip (code and name), one-line reason from the latest record, actions.
Node id, group, spec book pointer (path and anchor), who acts for the current code (from the code table).
Status code, meaning, heartbeat age with a bar against the node's stall bound (N-12), last record at.
Every wait of the node with its timeout and fallback, generated from the node volume's #waits; retries 3 then recover and report.
Current ticket id and full title, seat id and model, lease expiry and fencing token, attempt n of 3, bring-up time; empty text when no lease.
Input record kind and the latest one received; output record kind and the latest one written; belts in and out as links to neighbour machines.
The node's checklist items with their proof state: ticked with the proof pointer, or open; count done of total.
The last ten records this node wrote: at, kind, code, one line.
The last five alerts on this node: code, since, cause, what the system did; tap opens Alerts filtered to the node.
Runbook pointer (path and anchor), opens read-only in the repo viewer.
Open the runbook (primary), Jump to Alerts, Close panel; on the phone a bottom sheet.

mechanism.diagram: flowchart LR SEL[selection record: node id] --> V[client: subscribe node view on the same stream] P[N-31 pushed.frame: node state frame] --> V R[registry machines.json: anchors, kinds, waits text] --> V V --> D[machine.panel drawn] D -->|Open the runbook| RB[repo viewer, read-only] D -->|Jump to Alerts| AL[N-41 filtered to the node] D -->|Close panel| MAP[N-38] D -->|follow a belt| SEL2[selection record for the neighbour]

step.s: On a selection the client sends a view subscription on the open stream: view node, id N-xx; N-31 answers with the node's state frame as a full view and then deltas scoped to that node (shared need: N-31 view subscriptions by node id). The map's own stream stays open underneath so Close panel is instant.

The header lamp and chip come from the latest record code and the code table (meaning, who acts, lamp); the one-line reason is the record's message field; the heartbeat bar divides age by the node's stall bound (from N-12's config in the registry) and turns red past 1.0.
The checklist panel joins the node volume's #checklist items (static) with checklist.state records (which ticket ticked which item with which proof pointer); an item with no record is open.
Open the runbook opens the repository viewer at the runbook anchor (GitHub now, Forgejo later, D18) in a new tab; the panel never embeds the repository.
The panel is part of the same bundle as N-38, bound by N-37, styled from look.json, served by the tiers and the pod; there is no separate deploy.

states.state: Every panel filled for a stalled node (the approved frame shows merge stalled 39 h with ST code, cause, checklist 2 of 5, last five alerts, runbook), including one longest-plausible ticket title to expose truncation.

A node that has never written a record: grey lamp, status never ran, the explanation that the node ships dark until its own ticket lights it, and the primary recovery action Open the spec as a real button.
Skeleton blocks in the shape of the default panels; no centred spinner; until the node view arrives or the timeout fires.
not-found (the node id is not in the registry: a stale link), timeout (no node view within 10 s), validation (the view failed schema); what to do next and Retry.
The last node view stays with the as-of stamp; actions that write (follow a belt) queue with the indicator; Open the runbook still works because it is a link.

start.s: Opens on a selection record from N-38 or N-41 and on a deep link /board#machine/N-xx; the view subscription is sent by the client; nothing is typed by an agent. Ships with the N-38 bundle and is promoted by N-48.

wait.name: node-view-first-frame
wait.fallback: error state class timeout with Retry; the map underneath stays live
wait.s: From the subscription to the node's full view.

wait.name: node-view-staleness
wait.fallback: stale chip (503) on the panel; at 60 s offline banner; last view stays
wait.s: Deltas or the idle heartbeat from N-31 at least every 5 s.

wait.name: runbook-link
wait.fallback: the link is a plain anchor; if the forge is down the browser shows it, the panel does not block

wait.name: selection-ack
wait.fallback: resend with the same idempotency key up to 3 times, then queue and resend on reconnect
wait.s: Following a belt writes a selection record like N-38.

wait.name: unknown-node
wait.fallback: error state class not-found with a Back to map button
wait.s: A node id not in machines.json (a stale deep link after a registry change).

retries.s: Client steps retry up to 3 with backoff then recover into a visible state (offline, queued action, not-found); the panel never loops silently. Build and promotion failures are N-11's and N-48's three attempts.

many-agents.s: Readers: every client has its own selection and its own node view subscription; two clients looking at two nodes cost two scoped subscriptions on one transport; two clients looking at the same node receive the same deltas independently.

The panel shows many agents on one node truthfully: when a node has several leases (two attempts of two tickets on N-16 at once), the ticket-seat panel lists every lease with its fencing token and expiry, never a single current seat; the header says 3 seats where the map shows 3 inserters.

Writes: selection records only, idempotent by client id and counter; a retried send with the same request replays 200 at N-01 (shared/contracts.xml#operation-keys), a no-op. No panel state is shared between clients; a seat that opens the Machine screen for a screenshot never changes what the owner sees.
Conflict detection: a node view whose seq is lower than the map's delivered seq for the same node is dropped and the client asks for a full view (never shows older data than the map).

status-codes.code: A belt was followed and the selection landed.
Node id not in the registry; error state not-found.
Node view failed schema; full view requested; alert raised by the transport.
No delta or heartbeat within 10 s.
No node view within 10 s; error state timeout, retrying.

state-paths.path: Selection records written when a belt is followed (shared with N-38).

path.cleanup: N-45 retention class: keep 7 days, then hourly aggregates

state-paths.s: The panel writes no files; the screenshots for promotion are N-38's path.

look.requirement: owner 04:45Z: all views carry the Krastorio look; note 6 same on phone
look.s: The panel is the Factorio entity window: outer frame #313031 with the 24 px header strip and caption #FFE6C0 Titillium Web Bold 18, inside shallow frames #403F40 for the cards, deep #242324 for the record and alert lists, the big lamp as a 40 px slot with glow, the heartbeat bar as the heat progress bar (#DA4535 past the bound, #2BE327 under), mono numbers in IBM Plex Mono, the machine icon from the atlas (Krastor entity icons 64 x 64, inventory section 5.2).
Check: look-check.mjs samples the panel header, the card interior and the lamp; binding-check rule look-token; the screenshot pair read by the architect.

item.proof: Ten screenshots on the promotion record read by the architect.

item.proof: Tests silencing the view, delaying it and using an unknown id.

permissions.s: Build seat: writes tools/map/src/machine/**, the Machine #panels of this volume, and tests; declared at cut.
Viewer and owner keys both read the panel; no action on this screen writes anything but a selection.

monitoring.s: The panel is the owner's drill-down; its own health is in frame.report like the map. A 404 for a node that is in index.xml but not in machines.json is a registry defect and an alert (N-41) on N-37.

runbook.s: Deep link for a test: /board#machine/N-12 on a dev tier; the view subscription is visible in the stream log of the tier server.
Cleanup: none beyond N-38's; the panel writes no files.
